# Getting started

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/getting-started.html
Source file: README.md

> **Status: P1 alpha.** The server, editor, database and whiteboard blocks, and
> the sample host all run end to end. See [the tracker](docs/10-EXECUTION-TRACKER.md)
> for what is done and what is open.

## How it fits

```
Your app  ── signs launch token (who, which file, which role) ──▶ OpenCanvas iframe
          ◀── load / save / assets / members / copies callbacks ──  OpenCanvas server
```

- **You own** authentication, users, ACL, files, versions and retention.
- **OpenCanvas owns** the editor, real-time merge (Yjs CRDT), presence and cursors,
  preview, export, and autosave back to your storage.
- **OpenCanvas keeps nothing** once a session is saved and idle. Its database only
  holds the transient room log and the save outbox.

## What works today

| Area | Status |
|---|---|
| Blocks | Text, headings, lists, checklists, toggles, quotes, callouts, code, simple tables, images, files, link cards, sandboxed embeds, columns |
| Databases | Typed fields; table, board (kanban), calendar and gallery views; filter, sort and search; row detail; CSV import and export |
| Whiteboard | Pen, sticky notes, shapes, text, arrows that stay attached to shapes, images, zoom and full screen, live pointers, SVG and PNG export |
| Collaboration | Live co-editing, cursors with names, avatars, follow mode, comments, view, comment and edit roles enforced on the server |
| Saving | Autosave only, with no save button. Saves go through a durable outbox. Conflicts are handled by either saving a copy or reloading. |
| Templates | 40 templates in 9 categories, plus blank canvas, database, whiteboard and import |
| Integration | HS256, RS256, EdDSA and JWKS launch tokens; signed callbacks; live role changes; `<open-canvas>` SDK; postMessage API |
| Storage | SQLite by default. MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.4 work when `DATABASE_URL=mysql://…` is set. |
| Mobile | Side-panel and phone layouts, bottom sheets, an editing toolbar above the keyboard, and touch-friendly whiteboard and kanban |

## Run it

You need Rust (stable), Node 24 and pnpm 9.

```sh
cd web && pnpm install && pnpm --filter @opencanvas/editor build && cd ..
OC_DEV=1 cargo run --release -p oc-server     # http://localhost:8080
node examples/sample-host/server.mjs          # http://localhost:4000
```

Open http://localhost:4000 and open a file. In a second tab, pick another user under
"Signed in as" and open the same file to see live collaboration. Use the "Access
control" column to change roles while people are editing.

To review the UI without a backend, use the editor in demo mode: run
`pnpm --filter @opencanvas/editor dev` and open `http://localhost:5173/app/#demo`.

`docker compose up --build` runs both services. `OC_DEV=1` allows starting without
`OC_KEK`. In production, set `OC_KEK` (32 bytes, base64) and the other variables listed
in [docs/13](docs/13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md).

## Embed it

```html
<script type="module" src="https://canvas.example.com/sdk/embed.js"></script>
<open-canvas server="https://canvas.example.com" token="{{ launch_jwt }}" style="height:100vh"></open-canvas>
```

The host contract (token claims, callbacks, postMessage events and REST) is in
[docs/05](docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md). [docs/15](docs/15-BUILD-CONTRACT.md) has
the exact wire formats.

## Test

```sh
OC_DEV=1 cargo test --workspace                  # server, room protocol, role filter, outbox, fuzz
cd web && pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm -r test      # editor, database, board
scripts/e2e-db.sh sqlite                         # launch → edit → autosave → export
scripts/e2e-db.sh mysql mysql://root:root@127.0.0.1:33062/opencanvas
```


# FAQ

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/faq.html

## FAQ

Short answers, with links to the pages that say more.

## Can I use it in production today?

Not yet. OpenCanvas is a P1 alpha for evaluation. The server, the editor, the database and whiteboard blocks and the sample host run end to end, and most work is built and verified, but it still awaits the owner's review and there is no tagged release. The roadmap shows each item's status.

## What does the licence allow?

OpenCanvas is source-available under the Business Source License 1.1 (BUSL-1.1), with CasualOffice as the licensor. Allowed at no cost: running it in production, self-hosting it, and embedding it in your own products and services, whether those are open or closed source, commercial or not. Needs a commercial licence: offering OpenCanvas to others as a hosted or managed service whose main purpose is collaborative editing of documents, databases or whiteboards. Later: each version becomes available under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 four years after it is first published under BUSL-1.1. The LICENSE file states the exact terms and is the authority; this summary is not legal advice. For other arrangements, contact the licensor through the repository.

## Does OpenCanvas keep my documents?

Only while a session is live. The server keeps a snapshot and the recent updates so it survives a restart and late joiners can catch up, and deletes them after the session is saved and idle. The file lives in your app; OpenCanvas writes it back there. See Architecture .

## How do users sign in?

To your app, not to OpenCanvas. Your backend checks access and signs a short-lived launch token naming the file, the user and the role (view, comment or edit). OpenCanvas trusts that decision for the life of the token, enforces it on every edit, and switches a user's role live when your app calls the role API. See the integration guide .

## Is there a Save button?

No. Every change saves to your app on a short timer, when the canvas goes idle, when the last person leaves and when the server shuts down. Saves go through a durable outbox, so a restart resends them. If your copy of the file changed elsewhere, your chosen policy runs: save a copy, or reload.

## We already use Collabora through WOPI. Can we reuse that?

Yes. OpenCanvas is a WOPI client: discovery, CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile and PUT_RELATIVE, with an allow-list for the WOPISrc URLs it will call. Proof keys are not supported yet. See WOPI mode .

## What can it import and export?

Export: Markdown, HTML, JSON, the native .ocanvas file, Word, and PDF when the operator runs the optional Gotenberg sidecar (otherwise the editor prints to PDF). Whiteboards export as SVG and PNG. Import: Markdown, HTML and CSV. See Operations .

## How does it scale?

One node runs on SQLite. For more users, run several nodes against MySQL or MariaDB with Redis: each room has one owner node, other nodes relay to it, and if the owner dies another node takes the room over from its log. See Operations and Architecture .

## Does the demo send anything anywhere?

No. The demo is the real editor running against a document in your browser, with simulated collaborators. There is no server behind it, and exports that need a server say so.


# Integration guide

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/integration.html
Source file: docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md

**Status:** draft v0.1, 2026-11-21. This is the contract an integrating
application implements. Modelled on Collabora Online's WOPI integration
([01 §4](01-RESEARCH-COMPETITIVE-ANALYSIS.md)).

> **Golden rule:** your application decides *who* may open *which* file with
> *what* role. OpenCanvas trusts that decision for the life of the token and
> enforces it on every edit. Your application stores the file.

## 1. Choose a handshake

| | **JWT launch** (recommended for new apps) | **WOPI-compatible** (for existing WOPI hosts) |
|---|---|---|
| Who verifies the user | You sign a JWT | OpenCanvas calls your CheckFileInfo |
| Callbacks you implement | `GET file`, `PUT file`, assets (people search and resolve optional) | WOPI: CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile |
| Extra round-trip on open | none | CheckFileInfo |
| Good for | Any custom app | Nextcloud, ownCloud, Seafile-style hosts |

## 2. Register your host

`opencanvas.hosts.toml` (or `hosts` table):
```toml
[[host]]
id              = "acme"
name            = "Acme"
mode            = "jwt"                    # jwt | wopi | both
jwt_alg         = "HS256"                  # or RS256 / EdDSA: jwt_public_key (PEM) or jwt_jwks_url
jwt_secret      = "env:ACME_OC_SECRET"
api_key         = "env:ACME_OC_API_KEY"    # for server→server REST calls to us
callback_base   = "https://api.acme.example/opencanvas"
allowed_origins = ["https://app.acme.example"]
asset_origins   = ["https://cdn.acme.example"] # extra image origins for exports (unsigned GET);
                                           # your callback_base origin is always allowed
[host.flags]
embeds          = ["youtube", "vimeo", "loom", "figma", "maps"]
export_formats  = ["md", "html", "pdf", "ocanvas"]
autosave_secs   = 60
on_conflict     = "copy"                   # copy | reload
```

People (docs/21 revision 2): the @mention list is the people with access to the canvas, the same
for every viewer. Everyone with access sees real names and the `detail` second line. OpenCanvas
never shows or stores e-mail.

## 3. JWT launch token

Signed by your backend, short-lived (≤ 10 h; 5–15 min recommended — it is
exchanged for a session ticket on open).

```json
{
  "iss": "acme",                    // = host id
  "aud": "opencanvas",
  "exp": 1763730000,
  "jti": "9f1c…",                   // single-use
  "file": {
    "id": "doc_8812",               // your stable id
    "name": "Sprint 42 notes",
    "version": "17",                // your current version/etag
    "context": { "type": "channel", "id": "c_55" }   // optional, for UI only
  },
  "user": {
    "id": "u_123",                  // stable, opaque: the identity (names are display only)
    "name": "Asha Rao",
    "detail": "Design · Bengaluru", // optional second line that tells same-named people apart
    "avatar": "https://…/a.png",    // http(s) only
    "color": "#7c3aed"              // optional; we derive one otherwise
  },
  "members": [                      // optional (docs/21): everyone with access to THIS canvas,
    { "id": "u_200", "name": "Ravi Menon", "detail": "Engineering" }   // ≤ 500; same user shape
  ],                                // (id, name, detail?, avatar?, color?); never e-mail
  "role": "edit",                   // view | comment | edit
  "perms": {
    "export": true,
    "download": true,
    "print": true,
    "commitMessage": true,          // may write "Save version" messages
    "mention": true
  },
  "mode": "edit",                   // edit | view | preview
  "callbackToken": "opaque-…"       // we send it back on every callback; you validate it
}
```

## 4. Embed in your page

### Option A — iframe form POST (works everywhere, like Collabora)
```html
<form id="oc" target="oc-frame" method="post"
      action="https://canvas.example.com/v1/launch">
  <input type="hidden" name="token" value="{{ jwt }}">
</form>
<iframe name="oc-frame" style="width:100%;height:100%;border:0"
        allow="clipboard-read; clipboard-write; fullscreen"></iframe>
<script>document.getElementById('oc').submit()</script>
```

### Option B — web component
```html
<script type="module" src="https://canvas.example.com/sdk/embed.js"></script>
<open-canvas server="https://canvas.example.com" token="{{ jwt }}"
             theme="auto" style="height:100vh"></open-canvas>
<script>
  const oc = document.querySelector('open-canvas');
  oc.addEventListener('oc:ready',  e => {});
  oc.addEventListener('oc:saved',  e => console.log(e.detail.commitId));
  oc.addEventListener('oc:presence', e => console.log(e.detail.users));
  oc.addEventListener('oc:error',  e => {});
  oc.addEventListener('oc:token-expiring', async e => oc.refresh(await myApi.newToken()));
  await oc.commit({ message: 'Final' });
  oc.setReadOnly(true);
</script>
```

The SDK is served with CORS for the host's `allowed_origins` only, and the canvas sets
`frame-ancestors` to the same list: register every origin your pages embed from.

### postMessage API (iframe ↔ host page)
Messages are `{ "MessageId": "...", "SendTime": ms, "Values": {...} }`
(Collabora-compatible envelope).

| Direction | MessageId | Values |
|---|---|---|
| canvas → host | `App_LoadingStatus` | `{ Status: "Frame_Ready" \| "Document_Loaded" }` |
| canvas → host | `Doc_ModifiedStatus` | `{ Modified: bool }` |
| canvas → host | `Doc_Saved` | `{ commitId, hostVersion }` |
| canvas → host | `Presence_Changed` | `{ users: [{id,name,color,role,detail?}] }` (real names, the same for every viewer; never e-mail) |
| canvas → host | `Token_Expiring` | `{ inSeconds }` |
| canvas → host | `UI_Mention_Click` / `UI_Link_Click` | `{ id \| url }` (host decides navigation) |
| canvas → host | `UI_BlockLink` | `{ fileId, blockId }` ("Copy link to block": the host builds its own URL, e.g. `https://app/files/<fileId>#block=<blockId>`; ADR-023/027). The same values are also posted as `UI_Block_Link`, the earlier name; new hosts listen to `UI_BlockLink` only. |
| canvas → host | `Error` | `{ code, message }` |
| host → canvas | `Host_PostmessageReady` | `{}` |
| host → canvas | `Action_Commit` | `{ message? }` |
| host → canvas | `Action_SetReadOnly` | `{ readOnly }` |
| host → canvas | `Action_RefreshToken` | `{ token }` |
| host → canvas | `Action_Export` | `{ format }` |
| host → canvas | `Action_Theme` | `{ theme: "light"\|"dark"\|tokens }` |
| host → canvas | `Action_ScrollToBlock` | `{ blockId }`: scroll to the block and flash it (1.8 s; a steady outline with reduced motion). Unknown ids show "That block isn't in this canvas any more". |

Origins are checked against `allowed_origins` both ways.

**Links to a block.** Your link is your URL (OpenCanvas never shows one of its own inside a
host). To open the canvas at a block, either pass `block=<blockId>` to the launch (a form field
next to `token`, or `?block=` on `/v1/launch`; anything but `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` is dropped) and
the editor opens with `#t=…&block=<id>`, or send `Action_ScrollToBlock` once the frame has loaded.
`examples/sample-host` does both: its file page reads `#block=` from its own URL into the launch
form, and its Mentions list sends `Action_ScrollToBlock`.

## 5. Callbacks you implement (JWT mode)

Base: `callback_base`. Every call carries `Authorization: Bearer <callbackToken>` and
`X-OpenCanvas-Signature: t=<ts>,v1=<hex>,v2=<hex>` so you can verify the call comes from
OpenCanvas:

- `v2` = hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, `"<ts>.<METHOD>.<path?query>.<body>"`). Verify this one. It
  binds the request method and path, so a captured signature can't be replayed against
  another endpoint.
- `v1` = hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, `"<ts>.<body>"`), kept for hosts written before v2.
- Reject timestamps more than 5 minutes off, and compare in constant time.
- OpenCanvas never follows redirects from your callbacks: answer directly.

`examples/sample-host/server.mjs` verifies `v2`.

| Call | Request | Response |
|---|---|---|
| **Load file** `GET /files/{fileId}` | — | `200` body = `.ocanvas` / `.md` / `.html` bytes, headers `Content-Type`, `ETag: "<version>"`. `404` → new empty canvas. |
| **Save (commit)** `PUT /files/{fileId}` | body `.ocanvas`; headers `If-Match: "<version>"`, `Idempotency-Key: <commitId>`, `X-OpenCanvas-Commit-Message`, `X-OpenCanvas-Authors: <json>`, `X-OpenCanvas-Autosave: 0|1` | `200 {"version":"18"}`; `409 {"version":"19"}` if your file changed outside the session; `413` too large. |
| **Save as copy** `POST /files/{fileId}/copies` (conflict policy `copy`) | body `.ocanvas`; `Idempotency-Key` | `201 {"fileId":"doc_9001","url":"…"}` (create it with the original's ACL) |
| **Upload asset** `POST /files/{fileId}/assets` | multipart `file` | `201 {"assetId":"a_1","url":"https://…","mime":"image/png","size":1234}` |
| **Get asset** `GET /files/{fileId}/assets/{assetId}` | — | bytes or `302` to a signed URL |
| **Members** *(optional, docs/21)* `GET /files/{fileId}/members?q=&limit=` | signed like every callback, with the `callbackToken` of whoever asked; cached 60 s per file, dropped at once by a revoke (§7) or `POST /v1/files/{fileId}/members/invalidate` | `[{"id","name","detail","avatar","color"}]` (or `{"members":[…]}`, ≤ 500): everyone with access to this file whose name or detail matches `q` (empty = everyone). `404`/`405`/`410`/`501` = not implemented; any e-mail you send is ignored |
| **Refresh token** *(optional)* `POST /tokens/refresh` | `{fileId,userId}` | `{ "token": "<new jwt>" }` |
| **Mentions** *(optional)* `POST /mentions` | JSON `{fileId, blockId?, threadId?, mentioned:[userId], by:userId, excerpt}`; header `Idempotency-Key` | any `2xx`. `404`/`405`/`410`/`501` = not implemented (never retried) |

**Mentions** (ADR-027). When someone @mentions people in a comment, or puts a mention chip in
the canvas text, we tell you so you can notify them (we never send mail or push ourselves).
One call per comment message, and one per block per edit for text mentions; `threadId` is set
for comments, `blockId` for text (the editor gives the block an id when the mention is
inserted, so you can link to it). `by` is the user whose connection wrote it (from the grant,
not from the document); the author is never in `mentioned`. `excerpt` is the message or block
text, at most 280 characters. A mention that was already in the file when the room loaded, or
one the editor re-creates when a paragraph is split or moved, is not sent again. The ids in
`mentioned` come from the canvas's member list (your token `members` or `GET /files/{fileId}/members`): **check that each person
can see the file before you notify them.** Delivery is fire-and-forget for the session: the call
is written to our notification outbox first, sent at once, and retried with backoff (10 s → 1 h,
8 attempts, same `Idempotency-Key`) when it fails with a network error, `429` or `5xx`. Any other
`4xx` drops it. Signed like every callback. `examples/sample-host` logs each call and lists them
on the file page. **WOPI hosts get no mention calls** (WOPI has no notification API); use JWT
mode, or `mode = "both"`, if you need them.

**People** (docs/21 revision 2, ADR-026). Every person is keyed by your stable `user.id`. The
@mention list is **the people with access to this canvas**, the same for every viewer. Tell
OpenCanvas who that is with `members` in the launch token (≤ 500) and/or the members callback
above (for large audiences). Without either, the list is everyone who has opened the canvas (the
`people` map in the `.ocanvas`: id, name, detail, avatar, last seen). Members merge by id:
**callback > token > the saved `people` map**. Everyone with access sees real names and the
`detail` second line; same-named people show `name · detail` (then "Last here …", then the id's
last 4 characters). E-mail is never shown or stored. A mention stores the id plus a label
snapshot: OpenCanvas shows the member's current name, and for someone who no longer has access
the snapshot with "No longer has access". Exports use the same names.

Timeouts: 10 s (load/save), 5 s (others). Retries with exponential backoff
for save (idempotent by `Idempotency-Key`). A save is written to our commit outbox before
we call you, so it is retried with the same key even across a restart of OpenCanvas.

With `jwt_jwks_url` we fetch your JWKS (cached 10 min) and pick the key by the token's `kid`;
the algorithm is still pinned by `jwt_alg`, so a token signed with another algorithm is refused.

## 6. WOPI mode

WOPI mode has its own page: [WOPI mode](wopi.html).

## 7. Server-to-server REST (you → us)

Use `X-OpenCanvas-Key: <api_key>` + `X-OpenCanvas-Host: <host id>`.

- Revoke or downgrade a user live when you change ACLs:
  `POST /v1/files/{fileId}/role {"userId":"u_123","role":"view"}` — the
  user's open session switches to read-only immediately (or is closed with
  `"role":"none"`). Roles: `view | comment | edit | none`. Answers
  `200 {"connections":1,"sessions":2}` (live connections switched, tickets updated);
  `401 API_KEY_INVALID` for a wrong host/key, `400 ROLE_INVALID`. `"role":"none"` also takes
  the user out of the canvas's member list at once (the cached members answer is dropped, open
  editors refetch it, and an older token's `members` no longer counts for them) until you grant
  access again or they open the canvas with a new token.
- Member list changed (someone added or removed outside a role call):
  `POST /v1/files/{fileId}/members/invalidate` → `200 {"invalidated":true}`. Drops the cached
  members answer; open editors refetch `/v1/members`. Same headers as every call here.
- Patch content from a bot: `POST /v1/files/{fileId}/patch` (see 04 §6) with
  `{"ops":[…],"author":{"id","name"}}`. Ops: `append`, `insertAfter{blockId}`,
  `replace{blockId}`, `delete{blockId}`, each with `markdown` or Tiptap `blocks`. Blocks are
  addressed by their `blockId` attribute; the answer lists the ids of the blocks you inserted
  (`{"applied":2,"blockIds":["b_…"],"live":true}`). If nobody has the file open we load it from
  you, apply and save straight away (the answer then carries `version`). Send
  `X-OpenCanvas-Callback-Token: <token>` if your callbacks need a bearer for that load/save.
- Force save before you snapshot/backup: `POST /v1/files/{fileId}/commit` →
  `200 {"live":true,"saved":true,"version":"18"}` once your `PUT` answered,
  `202 {"queued":true}` if it failed and will be retried from the outbox, `409` on a conflict.
- Close everything (file deleted/moved): `DELETE /v1/files/{fileId}/session` — a final
  save, then every connection is closed and every ticket for the file is dropped.
  `200 {"closed":true,"sessions":3}`.
- Stateless conversion: `POST /v1/convert?from=md|html|ocanvas&to=ocanvas|md|html|json|docx|pdf`
  with the file as the raw body. DOCX and PDF embed images only from your `callback_base` origin
  (fetched signed) or an `asset_origins` entry (plain GET) — no redirects, ≤ 10 MB, `image/*`
  only; other images become links. Boards become pictures (PNG in DOCX, SVG in HTML/PDF).
  `to=pdf` needs the operator to run the Gotenberg sidecar (`OC_PDF_RENDERER`), else `501`.

## 8. Lifecycle & guarantees

- **One live room per (host, file).** Users who open the same file join the
  same room — there is no fork. The room loads your file once.
- **Your file is updated by commits only.** Autosave commits are flagged
  `X-OpenCanvas-Autosave: 1` so you can collapse them in version history.
- **At-least-once commit** with idempotency key; final commit before room
  close; on graceful shutdown all dirty rooms commit.
- **Nothing is retained** after the room closes and TTL passes.
- **Role changes** you make during a session take effect only when you call
  the role API or the token expires — tokens are the contract.

## 9. Checklist for integrators

- [ ] Register host, share secret/API key out of band.
- [ ] Backend endpoint that signs the launch JWT after *your* ACL check.
- [ ] Implement load / save (+ assets). People: give `user.detail` in the token; add
      `members` (≤ 500) and/or `GET /files/{fileId}/members` (docs/21); call the role API or
      `members/invalidate` when access changes.
- [ ] Verify `X-OpenCanvas-Signature` on callbacks.
- [ ] Add OpenCanvas origin to your CSP `frame-src`; add your origin to our `allowed_origins`.
- [ ] Handle `409` (we save a copy or reload, per your policy). With `copy`, implement
      `POST /files/{id}/copies`; editors are told the new file's `url` and the session
      turns read-only. With `reload`, the session's unsaved changes are dropped and everyone
      reconnects onto your version.
- [ ] Call the role API when ACLs change.
- [ ] Try `examples/sample-host` end-to-end before going live (WOPI hosts:
      `examples/wopi-host` and `scripts/e2e-wopi.sh`).


# WOPI mode

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/wopi.html
Source file: docs/05-INTEGRATION-GUIDE.md

For hosts that already open Collabora / Office Online through WOPI (Nextcloud, ownCloud,
Seafile, …). OpenCanvas is the WOPI *client*; you are the WOPI *host*. Reference host:
`examples/wopi-host/server.mjs`; end-to-end check: `scripts/e2e-wopi.sh`.

**Register** (no JWT key needed):
```toml
[[host]]
id              = "nextcloud"
name            = "Nextcloud"
mode            = "wopi"                    # or "both" (JWT launches + WOPI launches)
wopi_allowlist  = ["https://cloud.example.com/index.php/apps/richdocuments/wopi"]
allowed_origins = ["https://cloud.example.com"]
api_key         = "env:NC_OC_API_KEY"       # optional, for the §7 REST API
[host.flags]
on_conflict     = "copy"                    # copy = PUT_RELATIVE | reload
```
`wopi_allowlist` entries are `scheme://host[:port][/path]`. A `WOPISrc` is accepted only when
scheme, host and port match an entry exactly and the path starts with the entry's path at a
`/` boundary; URLs with userinfo, a query, a fragment, or longer than 255 characters are refused
(`403 WOPISRC_NOT_ALLOWED`) before anything is called. Write `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`
separately if you need both. Redirects are never followed.

**Discovery.** `GET /hosting/discovery` returns WOPI discovery XML (`net-zone`
`external-http(s)` from `OC_PUBLIC_URL`): app `application/vnd.opencanvas+zip` with `edit`
(default) and `view` for `ext="ocanvas"`, app `text/markdown` with `edit`, `view` and `convert`
(`targetext="ocanvas"`) for `ext="md"`, and `Capabilities` → `GET /hosting/capabilities`.
Every `urlsrc` is `{OC_PUBLIC_URL}/v1/launch?`; append `WOPISrc=<urlencoded>` (and any other
placeholders, which are ignored), Collabora style.

**Launch.** Your page form-POSTs `access_token` and `access_token_ttl` (ms since the epoch; 0 or
absent = 10 h) into an iframe at `/v1/launch?WOPISrc=<urlencoded https://host/wopi/files/<id>>`.
We answer `303 /app/#t=<ticket>`, like a JWT launch. The session expires at `access_token_ttl`.
`401 TOKEN_INVALID` when CheckFileInfo answers 4xx or the ttl has passed. The access token is
opaque to us, sealed at rest under `OC_KEK` like a callback token, sent only in the query string
of calls to `WOPISrc` (as WOPI requires), and never logged. The file id (room, REST API path) is
the normalized `WOPISrc`: URL-encode it in `/v1/files/{fileId}/…`.

**We call:**
- `GET  {WOPISrc}?access_token=…` → CheckFileInfo (at launch, on load, and before a save when the
  file name is not known). We read `BaseFileName`, `Size`, `Version`, `LastModifiedTime`, `UserId`,
  `UserFriendlyName`, `UserExtraInfo.avatar` (http(s) only), `UserExtraInfo.detail` (the
  person's second line, docs/21), `UserCanWrite`, `ReadOnly`,
  `UserCanNotWriteRelative`, `DisableExport`, `DisablePrint`, `HideExportOption` and our extension
  `OpenCanvas_UserCanComment`.
  Role: `UserCanWrite` and not `ReadOnly` → `edit`; else `OpenCanvas_UserCanComment` → `comment`;
  else `view`. Perms: `DisableExport` → no export, download or print; `HideExportOption` → no
  export; `DisablePrint` → no print (PDF). The tracked version is `LastModifiedTime`
  (`Version` is shown only when there is no `LastModifiedTime`, and then no timestamp is sent).
- `GET  {WOPISrc}/contents?access_token=…` → GetFile (≤ 100 MB). Empty body = new canvas.
  `.ocanvas` zip, or Markdown when `BaseFileName` ends in `.md`.
- `POST {WOPISrc}/contents?access_token=…` → PutFile, body `.ocanvas` (or Markdown for `.md` files —
  lossy for boards and databases), headers `X-WOPI-Override: PUT`,
  `X-COOL-WOPI-Timestamp: <LastModifiedTime we loaded / last saved>`, `X-COOL-WOPI-IsAutosave: true`,
  `X-COOL-WOPI-IsModifiedByUser: true`. Answer `200 {"LastModifiedTime":"…"}` (without it we ask
  CheckFileInfo). `409 {"COOLStatusCode":1010}` = the file changed elsewhere → your `on_conflict`
  policy runs (any other 409 is retried like an outage). Saves go through the same outbox,
  retries and autosave rules as JWT mode (docs/15 §7).
- `POST {WOPISrc}?access_token=…` with `X-WOPI-Override: PUT_RELATIVE`,
  `X-WOPI-SuggestedTarget: <UTF-7 "<name> (conflict copy).ocanvas">`, `X-WOPI-Size` → conflict copy
  (policy `copy`). Answer `{"Name","Url","HostEditUrl"|"HostViewUrl"}`; editors are told the
  `HostEditUrl` and `Url` without its token. Hosts that set `UserCanNotWriteRelative` should use
  `on_conflict = "reload"`.

No `LOCK`/`UNLOCK` (we use timestamps, like Collabora) and no proof keys yet.

**Assets.** WOPI has no asset API, so uploads (`POST /v1/assets?ticket=`) are kept with the room
and answered `201 {"assetId":"a_…","url":"/v1/assets/a_…","mime","size"}`. They are served by
`GET /v1/assets/:id?ticket=` (images inline, anything else as a download, `nosniff`, sandboxed)
and inlined into the saved `.ocanvas` as `assets/<id>` (stored) plus `assets/index.json`
(`{"<id>":{"mime","size"}}`); only assets the document still references are written. On load
they are read back out of your file. Limits: **10 MB per asset, 50 MB of assets per file**
(`413 ASSET_TOO_LARGE`); the whole zip stays under the 100 MB `.ocanvas` read limit. DOCX, PDF
and `.ocanvas` exports include them too.

**Mentions.** The member list is the users who have opened the file (from CheckFileInfo, with
their `detail`) and the saved `people` map: the no-source case of §5 "People". Mention notifications (`POST /mentions`, §5) are not sent in WOPI mode.


# Protocol and build contract

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/protocol.html
Source file: docs/15-BUILD-CONTRACT.md

**Status:** binding for the P1 build, 2026-11-21. If a builder needs to change
anything here, they update this file and say so in their report.

## 1. Repository layout

```
Cargo.toml                 Rust workspace
crates/oc-model            .ocanvas zip read/write, Yjs doc helpers, markdown/html export
crates/oc-server           axum binary `opencanvas`: config, host connector, store, rooms, autosave, routes
migrations/sqlite|mysql    identical logical schema (docs/04 §5)
web/packages/ui            design tokens (tokens.css) + shared TS types (BlockEnv, OcUser, Role)
web/packages/editor        Vite + React app: shell, Tiptap editor, gallery, comments, mobile bar
web/packages/database      React database block (table / board / calendar / gallery, CSV)
web/packages/board         React whiteboard block
examples/sample-host       Node reference host (JWT signing + callbacks + file store)
examples/wopi-host         Node reference WOPI host (CheckFileInfo/GetFile/PutFile/PutRelative)
```

The server serves the built editor (`web/packages/editor/dist`) at `/app/`.
`OC_WEB_DIR` overrides the path.

## 2. Launch flow

1. Host page form-POSTs `token=<JWT>` to `POST /v1/launch`.
2. Server verifies the JWT (docs/05 §3, HS256 via the host's `jwt_secret`), creates
   a session row, and answers `303 See Other` → `/app/#t=<ticket>`.
   (The ticket goes in the fragment so it never appears in server logs or Referer headers.)
   `GET /v1/launch?token=` does the same, for hosts that use a plain iframe `src`.
3. The SPA reads `#t`, calls `GET /v1/sessions/<ticket>` → `200`:
   ```json
   { "ticket":"01J…", "room":"r_7k…", "role":"edit",
     "user": {"id":"u_123","name":"Asha Rao","color":"#7a45f0","avatar":null},
     "file": {"id":"doc_8812","name":"Sprint 42 notes"},
     "host": {"id":"acme","name":"Acme"},
     "perms": {"export":true,"download":true,"comment":true,"print":true},
     "isNew": true,
     "wsUrl": "ws://localhost:8080/v1/collab" }
   ```
   `isNew` is true when the host returned 404 / an empty file. The SPA then shows
   the template gallery.
   *(docs/21 revision 2)*: `user` is `{id, name, color, avatar, detail?}`, never an e-mail. A `GET`
   lifts a role-API revoke for that viewer (a fresh token means access). `401 {"error":{"code":"TICKET_INVALID"}}` when unknown or expired.
   (Implementation: `isNew` = the room's doc has no `content` and empty `meta`/`databases`/`boards`,
   so a second user joining after a template was picked gets `false`.)
   Launch failures answer `401 {"error":{"code":"TOKEN_INVALID"|"TOKEN_REUSED",…}}`; `jti` is
   single-use per host (table `launch_jti`). The algorithm is pinned by the host entry
   (`jwt_alg` = `HS256` with `jwt_secret`, or `RS256`/`EdDSA` with `jwt_public_key` PEM or
   `jwt_jwks_url`; JWKS is cached 10 min, the token's `kid` must match a key whose type fits
   `jwt_alg`, an unknown `kid` refetches at most every 30 s), `aud` must be
   `opencanvas`, `iss` the host id, `exp` at most 10 h ahead, `nbf` honoured, 30 s leeway.
   **WOPI launch** (docs/05 §6, added 2026-11-21): `POST /v1/launch?WOPISrc=<urlencoded>` with form
   `access_token` (+ `access_token_ttl`, ms since the epoch) for a host with `mode = "wopi" | "both"`
   whose `wopi_allowlist` admits the URL (else `403 WOPISRC_NOT_ALLOWED`); CheckFileInfo decides
   role, user and perms (`401 TOKEN_INVALID` when it answers 4xx). Same `303`. The ticket lives
   until `access_token_ttl` (10 h when absent). `GET /hosting/discovery` (XML) and
   `GET /hosting/capabilities` (JSON). A JWT for a `mode = "wopi"` host is refused.
   **Open at a block** (UX-02): a `block` form field (or `?block=` query) on either launch adds
   `&block=<id>` to the fragment (`/app/#t=<ticket>&block=<id>`) when it matches
   `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`; the editor scrolls to that block and flashes it.
4. Tickets live for the launch token's `exp`. The WS must connect within 60 s of the
   first `GET /v1/sessions`, though reconnects with the same ticket are allowed until `exp`.

## 3. Collaboration WebSocket

`GET /v1/collab/<room>?ticket=<ticket>`, upgraded to a WebSocket. This is compatible with
the stock `y-websocket` `WebsocketProvider(wsUrl, room, doc, { params: { ticket } })`.

Binary frames, y-protocols encoding (lib0 varuint message type first):

| type | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | sync: 0 = step1, 1 = step2, 2 = update |
| 1 | awareness update |
| 2 | auth: the server sends `[2, 0 (permission denied), varString reason]` when a write is rejected |
| 3 | query awareness (client → server; the server answers with all awareness states) |
| 100 | OpenCanvas control: varString JSON, both directions |

(Changed 2026-11-21 by the server build: auth is type **2** and query-awareness is 3, as in
y-protocols / y-websocket and yrs. The earlier draft said 3 for auth.)

Server → client control JSON:
`{"t":"saving"}`, `{"t":"saved","at":<epoch ms>,"version":"18"}`,
`{"t":"save_error","retryInMs":10000,"message":"…"}`,
`{"t":"conflict","policy":"copy","fileId":"doc_9001","url":"…"}` (room stays read-only; joiners
get it as the save state),
`{"t":"conflict","policy":"reload"}` (followed by `closed` and close code 1012: the client must
drop its local Y.Doc and reconnect, the room now holds the host's version),
`{"t":"role","role":"view"}` (also sent mid-session when the host changes the role),
`{"t":"closed","reason":"…"}` (`access revoked` → close 1008; `closed by the host` → close 1000),
`{"t":"ping"}` (heartbeat every `OC_HEARTBEAT_MS`, default 10 s, on every connection; clients
treat 15 s without any frame as a lost connection, docs/06 §5; added 2026-11-21, UX-02),
`{"t":"reconnect"}` (always followed by close **1012**: the client keeps its Y.Doc and
reconnects; sent on graceful drain and, in cluster mode, when the room moved to another node).
(Changed 2026-11-21 by the server hardening: `conflict` carries `policy`.)
On connect the server sends sync step1 and the current awareness states. When the client's
step1 arrives the server answers with step2, then `{"t":"role",…}` and the current save state
(`saved` with the last known host version, or `saving`). Client → server control messages are
accepted and ignored for now.

Server rules:
- `view` role: sync step2 and update messages are dropped, and an auth frame is sent once.
- `comment` role: an update is accepted only if it touches nothing but the `comments` root
  (applied to a scratch copy of the doc first; updates that create other roots or cannot fully
  integrate are refused). The auth frame is sent once per connection.
- Awareness: the server rewrites the `user` field from the grant before fan-out
  (`{"id","name","color","avatar","detail"?}`), so nobody can spoof another person's name or colour.
  *(docs/21 revision 2)* Every recipient gets the same states: real names for everyone with access.
  Entries over 2 KB, or for a client id owned by another connection, are dropped.
- An update that would push the encoded doc over `OC_MAX_DOC_MB` (20) is refused with an auth
  frame `document size limit reached`; while a conflict is being handled every write is refused.
- Frames over `OC_MAX_FRAME_KB` (1024) close the socket with code 1009. More than 60 non-awareness
  frames/s (burst 120) closes it with **4429** `"rate limit"` (not 1008, which only means access
  revoked / session expired). Awareness frames (type 1) have their own bucket of 120/s (burst 240);
  excess awareness frames are dropped silently, never fatal. Clients should still batch (y-websocket
  awareness throttling, 50 ms update windows).
  (Changed 2026-11-21: was 1008 with awareness counted against the same bucket; fast typing tripped it.) When the ticket expires the server sends
  `{"t":"closed","reason":"session expired"}` and closes with 1008; on shutdown (SIGTERM drain)
  it commits dirty rooms, then sends `{"t":"reconnect"}` and closes with 1012.
  (Changed 2026-11-21 by CLU-01: was `{"t":"closed","reason":"server shutting down"}`.)
- Cluster mode (ADR-006): the socket may land on any node. A node that does not own the room
  relays it to the owner over an internal WebSocket; the protocol above is unchanged, roles
  are enforced by the owner. If the owner dies the client gets `reconnect` + 1012 (or a
  dropped socket) and reconnects with the same ticket.
- Room ids are `r_` + 26 lowercase base32 chars of sha256(`<hostId>:<fileId>`).

## 4. Y.Doc layout (shared by server export and web)

| root | type | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `content` | XmlFragment | Tiptap/ProseMirror document (`Collaboration` extension, `field: "content"`) |
| `meta` | Map | `title` string, `icon` lucide name, `tone` Tone, `template` id |
| `databases` | Map<dbId, Y.Map> | per database: `name`, `icon`, `tone`, `fields` Y.Array<Y.Map{id,name,type,options(JSON array)}>, `order` Y.Array<rowId>, `rows` Y.Map<rowId, Y.Map<fieldId,value>>, `notes` Y.Map<rowId,string>, `view` string, `views` Y.Map (per-view prefs JSON) |
| `boards` | Map<boardId, Y.Map> | `shapes` Y.Map<shapeId, Y.Map>, `order` Y.Array<shapeId> |
| `comments` | Map<threadId, Y.Map> | `quote`, `resolved`, `messages` Y.Array<Y.Map{user,name,color,text,at,mentions?,labels?}>; *(docs/21)* `labels` = `{userId: "@label as inserted"}`, so the text shows the member's current name in place of the inserted label |
| `people` | Map<userId, object> | *(docs/21, optional)* who opened the file: `{id, name, detail?, avatar?, lastSeen}` (ms), never an e-mail. Written by the server on join (never makes the room dirty; `lastSeen` refreshed at most hourly). The member list when the host gives neither token `members` nor the members callback; otherwise only fills a missing `detail`/`avatar` |

Tiptap node types (names are part of the file format, so don't rename them):
`paragraph, heading(level 1-3), bulletList, orderedList, listItem, taskList, taskItem(checked),
blockquote, codeBlock(language), horizontalRule, image(src,alt,caption), callout(tone,icon),
toggle(open) > toggleSummary + toggleContent, database(dbId), board(boardId),
bookmark(url,title,description,site), embed(provider,url,title), fileAttachment(name,size,url,mime),
columns > column, table/tableRow/tableHeader/tableCell, mention(id,label) inline,
commentMark(threadId) mark, dateMention(date) inline, textColor(color) mark`.

*(UX-02 / FILE-01 / LAY-01, ADR-027; all optional and additive, older clients keep them)*:
- `textColor(color)` mark: `color` ∈ `gray red amber green blue purple pink` (the tone tokens'
  `--<tone>-fg`, AA in light and dark). Anything else is ignored on parse and in exports.
  HTML `<span data-color="blue">`; exports: HTML inline `color` (light palette), DOCX run colour,
  Markdown plain text.
- `dateMention(date)` inline atom: `date` = `YYYY-MM-DD`. Shown as a chip ("Today", "Tomorrow",
  "Nov 24"); inserted with `@today`, `@tomorrow`, "Pick a date…" in the @ menu or `/date`.
  HTML `<span data-type="dateMention" data-date>` (parses `<time datetime>` too); exports:
  Markdown `2026-12-04`, HTML `<time datetime="2026-12-04">Dec 4, 2026</time>`, DOCX `Dec 4, 2026`.
- `fileAttachment` gains `display` (`card` | `preview`; absent = `preview` for PDFs, `card`
  otherwise) and `height` (inline preview height in CSS px, 240-1600; absent = 70 % of the
  viewport, at most 900). Exports never embed a viewer: HTML
  `<p class="oc-file" data-display><a>name</a> <span class="oc-file-meta">PDF · 2 KB</span></p>`,
  Markdown `[name](url) (PDF, 2 KB)`, DOCX a link.
- `columns` gains `widths` ("25,75": whole percents, one per column; absent = equal; 2-4
  columns; the editor snaps boundaries to quarters). `column` gains `title` (a label line above
  its blocks; absent = none). HTML exports the grid and a bold title line; Markdown a bold line.

**Block ids.** Any block node may carry an optional string attribute `blockId` (convention
`b_` + 26 lowercase base32 chars, e.g. `b_01jd…`). It is how the host patch API (§6) addresses
blocks; ids are unique within a document. Blocks the patch API inserts always get one (the
caller's `attrs.blockId` is kept, else one is generated). The editor must declare `blockId` as a
global attribute on block nodes (Tiptap `addGlobalAttributes`, default `null`, not rendered) and
keep it when a node is edited; a split keeps it on the first half only and pasting/duplicating
clears it. Without that, y-prosemirror drops the attribute the first time a user edits the block.
(Added 2026-11-21 by the server API build; the web part is still to do.)

**Board shape keys** (`boards/<id>/shapes/<shapeId>` Y.Map; all optional except `type`; source of
truth `web/packages/board/src/model.ts`). `type`: `sticky rect ellipse diamond text arrow pen swatch
image`. Geometry `x y w h` (numbers; `text` anchors at its first baseline), `pts` `[[x,y],…]` for
`arrow`/`pen`. Paint order is `order` (back to front; z-order buttons rewrite it), then any shape
missing from `order` by id.

| key | on | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `fill` | sticky | `y p b g` (default `y`) |
| `fill` | swatch | `accent amber green pink purple red blue` |
| `fill` | rect, ellipse, diamond | *(UX pass)* tone `gray blue green amber red purple pink`: fill `--<tone>-bg`, outline `--<tone>-fg`; unset or unknown = plain (`--app` fill) |
| `stroke` | pen, rect, ellipse, diamond | `"accent"` draws the outline/stroke in the accent colour (a tone `fill` wins for the outline) |
| `text` | sticky, rect, ellipse, diamond, text | the shape's text; `\n` breaks lines |
| `text` | arrow | *(UX pass)* connector label, trimmed, drawn in a pill at the path's midpoint |
| `size` | text | font size (default 18; UI offers 14 18 24 32) |
| `size` | rect, ellipse, diamond | *(UX pass)* text size (default 14, ellipse 15; UI offers 13 14 16 20), line height `round(size×1.3)` (ellipse `×1.27`) |
| `label` | rect | small uppercase corner label (frames) |
| `dashed` | rect | dashed frame, never filled |
| `group` | any | *(UX pass)* shapes with the same group id select and move together; no visual |
| `start`, `end` | arrow | `{shapeId, anchor}`, anchor `top right bottom left center` |
| `route` | arrow | `"elbow"` orthogonal route, `"straight"`/unset a line |
| `via` | arrow | *(open items, ADR-025)* manual waypoints `[[x,y],…]`, in order. The path runs end → waypoints → end; a `center`-bound end aims at the nearest waypoint (straight: outline toward it; elbow: the side facing it). Elbow with waypoints: each leg is an L (one corner), the first leaves along the start side's axis (else the leg's longer axis), each next leg leaves at a right angle to how the previous arrived, the last enters along the end side's axis (two corners at the leg's midpoint when an L can't). Entries that aren't arrays of ≥ 2 read as missing; non-numbers read as 0. Writers keep `pts` = the resolved path. Moving a connector with both bound shapes moves its waypoints too |
| `src`, `alt` | image | URL or `data:` URL; alt text |

Text wrapping *(UX pass)*: sticky, rect, ellipse and diamond text wraps greedily at whitespace to
`w − 28` (sticky, 14 px), `max(20, w − 16)` (rect), `max(20, w × 0.72)` (ellipse), `max(20, w × 0.6)`
(diamond); connector labels to 180 px at 12.5 px. Every UTF-16 unit counts `size × 0.56` px; longer
words are cut. A sticky's stored `h` grows on commit to `ceil(30 + (lines − 1) × 20 + 22)` and never
shrinks; exports apply the same rule. The web and Rust exporters implement this identically (shared
fixture `crates/oc-model/tests/fixtures/board.{json,web.svg}`).

Board awareness *(UX pass)*: `board` `{x, y, sel}`; `sel` lists the peer's selected shape ids, and
`board` may carry only `sel` while the pointer is outside the board.

**Database view prefs** (`databases/<id>/views` Y.Map, JSON per view name `table board calendar
gallery`; source `web/packages/database/src/types.ts` `ViewPrefs`): `q` search; `cal` calendar month
`YYYY-MM`; `filter` `{f, vals[]}` / `sort` `{f, dir: 1|-1}` (single rule, kept for older clients).
*(UX pass)*: `sorts` `[{f, dir}]` applied in order, wins over `sort` (writers keep `sort` = first);
`filters` `[{f, vals}]` ANDed, wins over `filter` (writers keep `filter` = first); `widths`
`{fieldId: px}` table column widths; `group` field id the board view groups by (status/select);
`date` field id the calendar places rows on; `cover` gallery cover: `"none"`, `"color"` (default) or
a URL field id.
*(Open items, ADR-025)*: `fields` field ids in this view's order (unknown ids ignored, fields missing
from it follow in the shared order; column moves write this, never the shared `fields` array);
`hidden` field ids hidden in this view (the title field is always shown). `filters` rules may be
typed: `{f, op, v?, v2?}` with `op` per field type — text/title/url `contains is empty` (case-insensitive,
on the cell's text); number/progress `eq ne lt le gt ge between empty` (`v`, `v2` numbers; `ne` also
matches empty cells; `between` is inclusive in either order); date `is before after` (`v` `YYYY-MM-DD`),
`next past` (`v` days, inclusive of today), `empty`. Status/select/tags/person/checkbox rules keep
`vals` (any of; checkbox `"true"`/`"false"`). Unfinished rules (no value yet, or an `op` the field type
doesn't take) are kept but filter nothing. `filter` mirrors the first `vals` rule only.

**Database field keys** (`fields` Y.Array of Y.Map): `id`, `name`, `type`, `options` (as above) and
*(ADR-025)* `description` — optional plain-text note (may be multi-line, absent when blank). Shown as a
header tooltip and in the row peek; exported in `document.json` (as stored) and as a footnote line
`*Field*: text` under the table in Markdown (web "Copy as Markdown" and the server export), not in CSV.

Field types for databases: `title text status select tags person date number checkbox url progress`.
Option objects: `{ "v": "In progress", "c": "blue" }`. Date values: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Person values: user id.

`.ocanvas` as written by the server: `manifest.json` (`format`, `version` 1, `schemaVersion` 1,
`createdWith`, `title` from `meta.title`, `commit {id, authors, at}`), `document.json` and `ydoc.bin`.
`ydoc.bin` is a Yjs **v1** update (`Y.encodeStateAsUpdate(doc)`); readers also accept v2.
`document.json` is `{type:"doc", content:[…], meta, databases, boards, comments, people?}` (`people` only
when non-empty) where `content`
nodes are `{type, attrs?, content?}` and text is `{type:"text", text, marks?:[{type, attrs?}]}`
(y-prosemirror `mark--hash` keys are reduced to `mark`). If `ydoc.bin` is missing the doc is built
from `document.json` (content and meta exactly; nested maps best-effort).

## 5. Host callbacks (JWT mode). The server calls the host.

Base `callback_base` from the host registry. Headers on every call:
`Authorization: Bearer <callbackToken from JWT>`,
`X-OpenCanvas-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(jwt_secret, "<t>.<body>")>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256(jwt_secret, "<t>.<METHOD>.<path?query>.<body>")>`.
(`v2` added 2026-11-21 by the security audit, ADR-022: it binds the method and path; hosts should
verify `v2` and may fall back to `v1`. Callbacks never follow redirects.)

| Call | Notes |
|---|---|
| `GET /files/{fileId}` | 200 bytes (`.ocanvas` zip, or `text/markdown`), `ETag`; 404 = new file |
| `PUT /files/{fileId}` | body `.ocanvas`; `If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key`, `X-OpenCanvas-Autosave: 1`, `X-OpenCanvas-Authors: <json ids>`; 200 `{"version":"…"}`, 409 conflict |
| `POST /files/{fileId}/assets` | multipart `file` → 201 `{"assetId","url","mime","size"}` |
| `GET /files/{fileId}/members?q=&limit=` *(optional, docs/21)* | signed GET with the asking viewer's `callbackToken`; `[user…]` or `{"members":[…]}` (≤ 500; `id`, `name`, `detail?`, `avatar?`, `color?`; any `email` ignored); cached 60 s per (room, q); 404/405/410/501 or a failure = no callback (token and saved map apply). The cache is dropped by `POST /v1/files/:id/role` with `none`, `DELETE /v1/files/:id/session` and `POST /v1/files/:id/members/invalidate` |
| `POST /files/{fileId}/copies` | conflict policy `copy`: body `.ocanvas`, `Idempotency-Key`; 200/201 `{"fileId","url"}` |
| `POST /mentions` *(optional)* | JSON `{fileId, blockId?, threadId?, mentioned:[userId], by, excerpt}`, `Idempotency-Key`; any 2xx; 404/405/410/501 = not implemented. Queued in `notify_outbox` first, retried with backoff (8 attempts). Never in WOPI mode (docs/05 §5) |

The HMAC key is the host's `callback_secret` if set, else `jwt_secret`. `If-Match` is the quoted
version from the last load/save (`ETag` of `GET`, else the JWT `file.version`). The PUT carries
`Content-Type: application/vnd.opencanvas+zip`; 412 is treated like 409. For uploads the multipart
body is forwarded byte for byte and the signature covers those bytes.
`OC_CALLBACK_BASE_OVERRIDE`, when set, replaces every host's `callback_base` (dev/compose only;
logged as a warning).

## 6. Server REST used by the SPA

`GET /v1/sessions/:ticket` · `POST /v1/assets?ticket=` (multipart, proxied to host; WOPI mode:
stored with the room, `201 {"assetId","url":"/v1/assets/<id>","mime","size"}`, ≤ 10 MB each, ≤ 50 MB
per file) · `GET /v1/assets/:id?ticket=` (WOPI mode only, else 404) ·
`GET /v1/members?ticket=&q=` → `{"members":[{id,name,color,detail?,avatar?}]}` (docs/21 revision 2:
the same list for every viewer; merged by id, members callback > token `members` > the saved `people`
map, which counts only when the host gave neither; the viewer is always in; people revoked by the
role API are left out; never e-mail) · `GET /v1/export/:fmt?ticket=` with `fmt` = `md|html|ocanvas|json|docx|pdf` (all but `ocanvas`
render mention labels and person cells with members' current names; non-members keep the stored label, docs/21) ·
`GET /v1/export/board/:boardId.svg|png?ticket=` · `GET /healthz` · `GET /readyz` · `GET /metrics`.

Host → server (docs/05 §7), headers `X-OpenCanvas-Host: <id>` + `X-OpenCanvas-Key: <api_key>`
(`api_key` in the host entry; 401 `API_KEY_INVALID` otherwise):
`POST /v1/files/:fileId/role {"userId","role":"view|comment|edit|none"}` → `{"connections","sessions"}`;
`DELETE /v1/files/:fileId/session` → final save, close all, drop tickets → `{"closed","sessions"}`;
`POST /v1/files/:fileId/patch` → `{"applied","blockIds","live"}` (+ `version` when no room was live);
`POST /v1/files/:fileId/commit` → `200 {"live","saved","version"}` / `202 {"queued":true}` / `409 CONFLICT`;
`POST /v1/convert?from=md|html|ocanvas&to=ocanvas|md|html|json|docx|pdf` (raw body in, file out).
Optional `X-OpenCanvas-Callback-Token`: the bearer used for callbacks made for that request (loading /
saving a file with no live room, fetching images); without it the bearer is empty and the host
authenticates the call by the HMAC signature. Details in docs/04 §6 and docs/05 §7.

DOCX (`export/docx`, `convert to=docx`): minimal WordprocessingML written with `zip` (no new crate).
Headings, marks, links (http/https/mailto only), bullet/numbered/task lists, quotes, code, tables,
callouts (shaded paragraphs), databases (caption + table), boards (a PNG rendered at 2×, shown at 1×,
caption "Whiteboard", alt text = the board's texts; a text note only if rendering fails),
bookmarks/embeds/files (links). Images that were not fetched (see *Images in exports*) become links.

Boards (`oc_model::board`, changed 2026-11-21): `to_svg(doc, boardId)` is a port of the web
`exportBoardSvg` (light palette, fitted to content + 32 px, stickies, rect/frame, ellipse, diamond,
swatch, text, pen, arrows incl. bound ends and elbow routes, images as `<image href>`); a parity test
compares it byte for byte with the web output. `to_png(svg, scale)` renders with `resvg` and the
embedded Geist Regular/SemiBold (OFL), no system fonts; only inline `data:` images are drawn (remote
URLs and file paths are never read); ≤ 16384 px a side, ≤ 64 Mpx. Exports: HTML inlines the board
SVG (`<figure class="board">`); Markdown keeps the note and, for ticketed exports, adds
`[Whiteboard (SVG)](<OC_PUBLIC_URL>/v1/export/board/<id>.svg?ticket=<ticket>)` (the link carries the
session ticket and stops working when it expires); `GET /v1/export/board/:boardId.svg` (image URLs
kept) / `.png` (allowed images inlined) need `perms.export`; unknown board 404 `BOARD_NOT_FOUND`.

PDF (ADR-010): `OC_PDF_RENDERER=gotenberg:<url>` → the print HTML is posted to Gotenberg's
`/forms/chromium/convert/html` (A4, 0.6" margins, backgrounds) and the PDF is streamed back
(`502 PDF_RENDERER_FAILED` if it fails). The print HTML is self-contained: allowed images and board
images inlined as `data:` URLs, other images are links, CSP `default-src 'none'; img-src data:` so the
renderer fetches nothing. Unset → `501 {"error":{"code":"PDF_RENDERER_NOT_CONFIGURED"}}` (the editor
uses its print stylesheet instead).

Images in exports (DOCX, board PNG, PDF): fetched only from allowed origins — the host's
`callback_base` origin (relative `/…` resolves there; signed + callback token), the original
`callback_base` origin while `OC_CALLBACK_BASE_OVERRIDE` is active (fetched through the override,
signed), and the host's `asset_origins = ["https://cdn…"]` (plain GET, no signature or token).
No redirects, ≤ 10 MB, `Content-Type: image/*` required, ≤ 50 per export; anything else is skipped.

`perms.print` (added 2026-11-21 with WOPI mode; JWT `perms.print`, WOPI `DisablePrint`, default
true) is additionally required for `pdf`.
`ocanvas` export needs `perms.download`, the others `perms.export` (403 otherwise); unknown formats
answer 404 `FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`. Exports carry `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<file name>.<ext>"`.
`POST /v1/assets` needs the `edit` role and `multipart/form-data` (≤ 25 MB); the host's status and
body are passed through. Every response carries `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`,
`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a CSP ending in `frame-ancestors 'self' <all hosts'
allowed_origins>`: by default `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
form-action 'self'; img-src 'self' https: http: data: blob:; …`; exports (`/v1/export/*`, `/v1/convert`)
are served with `sandbox; default-src 'none'; img-src data: https: http:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`,
room assets with `default-src 'none'; sandbox`. (Changed 2026-11-21 by the security audit, ADR-022.)
`GET /metrics` needs `Authorization: Bearer <OC_METRICS_TOKEN>` when that variable is set.
`GET /v1/members` refuses `q` over 200 bytes (`400 QUERY_TOO_LONG`). A room holds at most 550
connections (the next is closed with 1013 `room full`); a socket that stops reading is closed.

`GET /v1/assets/fetch?ticket=&url=` (FILE-01): an attachment's bytes served from this origin,
for previews (pdf.js and text previews can't read the host's origin). Same rules as export image
fetching: the URL must be on the host's `callback_base` origin (fetched signed) or an
`asset_origins` entry (plain GET), exact origin, no userinfo, never following redirects
(`403 ASSET_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `502 ASSET_UNAVAILABLE`, `404 ASSET_NOT_FOUND`). Streamed, at most
50 MB (`413 ASSET_TOO_LARGE`). Any role may preview (`perms.download` only hides the editor's
Download action; downloads keep the original URL). Answers with the real `Content-Type`,
`Content-Disposition: inline`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
`Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`. Room-served WOPI assets
(`/v1/assets/:id`) are already same-origin and are used as they are.

## 7. Autosave

No manual save anywhere (ADR-012). A room saves when it is dirty and:
- 2 s have passed since the last update (`OC_AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS`), or
- 10 s have passed since the first unsaved update (`OC_AUTOSAVE_MAX_MS`), or
- the last client leaves, or the process gets SIGTERM.

Saves are serialized per room. Each commit (`.ocanvas` bytes, idempotency key, base version,
sealed callback token) is written to `commit_outbox` as `pending` **before** the PUT; retries
resend the same row. 200 marks it `done` (payload dropped), 409 `conflict`, a newer commit marks
older pending rows `superseded`. A failure is retried with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 5 s, 10 s, …) and
sends `save_error`. At startup (and every 60 s) a sweeper reopens every room with a pending row
(from WAL, or from the outbox payload when there is no WAL) so the save continues after a restart.

A 409 stops autosave and applies the host's `[host.flags] on_conflict` (default `copy`):
`copy` → `POST /files/{id}/copies` with the room's state, then `conflict` with `fileId`/`url`;
the room is read-only and closes as soon as the last client leaves. `reload` → `GET` the
host's file, replace the room's state with it, send `conflict` + `closed`, close every socket.

Every accepted update is appended to `room_updates` before fan-out. A room writes the updates
that queued while its previous append ran as one batch (one row and `seq` per update, one
epoch-guarded statement, all or nothing), then fans them out in order; on SQLite one writer task
commits the batches of many rooms in one transaction (group commit, docs/22 §9.3). Every 500
updates or 30 s the
WAL is compacted into `room_snapshots`. A room that was dirty when the process died is rebuilt
from snapshot + WAL on the next join instead of reloading from the host. A clean room with no
clients for `OC_ROOM_TTL_SECS` (600) closes and its rows are purged.

WOPI mode (docs/05 §6): the same outbox and autosave; `HostClient` sends the save to the WOPI host
(PutFile with `X-COOL-WOPI-Timestamp` = the tracked `LastModifiedTime`; `409` + `COOLStatusCode`
1010 = conflict; policy `copy` = PUT_RELATIVE). The `saved` control's `version` is the host's
`LastModifiedTime`. Assets of a WOPI room live in `room_assets` (migration 0003) and are inlined as
`assets/<id>` + `assets/index.json` on every save; rows of rooms that are gone and have no pending
commit are swept by the 60 s sweeper (10 min grace).

## 8. Secrets and limits

`OC_KEK` (base64 of 32 bytes) seals the host callback token (in WOPI mode: the access token) in `sessions.grant_json` and
`commit_outbox.token` with AES-256-GCM (`enc:v1:<base64(nonce‖ct)>`, bound to the row id). The
server refuses to start without it unless `OC_DEV=1` (then tokens are stored in clear, with a
warning). `OC_MAX_DOC_MB` (20) caps the encoded document; 60 frames/s (burst 120) per socket.

Convergence fuzz: `cargo test -p oc-server --test fuzz` runs `OC_FUZZ_ITERS` (200) random rooms;
`OC_FUZZ_ITERS=10000 cargo test --release -p oc-server --test fuzz -- --nocapture` for the long
run, `OC_FUZZ_SEED=<n> OC_FUZZ_ITERS=1` to replay a failing seed.

## 9. Ports in dev

Server `:8080`, sample host `:4000`, Vite dev `:5173` (proxying `/v1` to `:8080`, ws included).


# Operations and deployment

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/operations.html
Source file: docs/13-OPERATIONS-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md

**Status:** draft v0.1, 2026-11-21. Implemented in SCAF-01 / OPS-01.

## Single node (default, SQLite)
```sh
docker run -p 8080:8080 -v oc-data:/data \
  -e OC_PUBLIC_URL=https://canvas.example.com \
  -e OC_KEK=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  -e OC_HOSTS_FILE=/data/opencanvas.hosts.toml \
  opencanvas/server:0.1
```
SQLite file at `/data/opencanvas.db` (WAL mode). Back it up only if you care
about un-committed edits surviving a disk loss — committed content is in the host.

## PDF export (optional Gotenberg sidecar, ADR-010)
```sh
docker run -d --name gotenberg gotenberg/gotenberg:8          # internal network only
-e OC_PDF_RENDERER=gotenberg:http://gotenberg:3000              # on the OpenCanvas container
```
Compose: `OC_PDF_RENDERER=gotenberg:http://gotenberg:3000 docker compose --profile pdf up`.
OpenCanvas sends Gotenberg self-contained HTML (images inlined, CSP `default-src 'none'`), so the
sidecar needs no route to hosts or the internet; keep it off public networks. Without it
`GET /v1/export/pdf` answers 501 and the editor prints from the browser. Board PNG/SVG and DOCX
need no sidecar (rendered in-process with `resvg`, see Fonts below).

## Fonts (board PNG, DOCX board images)
`oc_model::fonts` builds one font database per process on the first render (ADR-020):
embedded Geist (Latin) + subsets of Noto Sans Symbols 2 and Noto Sans Math (✓ ✗ → ⇒ ★ ☐ ⚠,
dingbats, shapes, arrows; ~270 KB), then system fonts, then every directory in `OC_FONT_DIRS`.
A character the board font lacks falls back to the symbol subsets, then Noto Sans / Noto Sans
CJK (SC, JP, KR, TC, HK) / other Noto families, then any face that has it. Characters no font
has render as boxes and log one `WARN` per script (`no font for this script`), never the text.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OC_FONT_DIRS` | image: `/opt/opencanvas/fonts` | Extra font directories, `:`-separated, searched recursively |
| `OC_SYSTEM_FONTS` | `1` | `0` skips system fonts (deterministic rendering, tests) |

The image installs Debian `fonts-noto-core` + `fonts-noto-cjk` (Sans only; Serif CJK removed),
so Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic, Thai and CJK render out of the box. Add
fonts by mounting them at `/opt/opencanvas/fonts`. Gotenberg (PDF) uses its own Chromium
fonts; `gotenberg/gotenberg:8` already ships Noto CJK and symbol fonts. `oc_model::fonts::coverage(text)`
lists the characters no loaded font can draw.

## Image
`docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t opencanvas .` — three stages: release binary
(`rust:1.98-slim-bookworm`), editor bundle (`node:24-slim`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`,
`pnpm --filter @opencanvas/editor build`), runtime `debian:bookworm-slim` with the binary, the
editor at `/srv/web` (served at `/app/`) and the fonts. Runs as uid 10001, works with a
read-only root filesystem (`--read-only --tmpfs /tmp` + a writable `/data` for SQLite).
`HEALTHCHECK` probes `/healthz` on port 8080 through bash's `/dev/tcp` (no curl in the image).
Size: 327 MB (binary 23 MB, editor 8 MB, fonts 80 MB, the rest Debian).

## Kubernetes (Helm)
Chart: `deploy/helm/opencanvas` (values documented inline; examples in `ci/`).
```sh
helm install oc deploy/helm/opencanvas --set secrets.kek=$(openssl rand -base64 32) \
  --set publicUrl=https://canvas.example.com --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.host=canvas.example.com \
  --set-file hosts.toml=opencanvas.hosts.toml
```
- **SQLite** (no `database.url`): exactly one replica, `Recreate` rollouts, `/data` on an
  emptyDir (or `persistence.enabled` for a PVC). The chart refuses `replicaCount > 1` or HPA.
- **Cluster**: `database.url` (or `database.existingSecret`) + `redis.url`; HPA optional
  (`autoscaling.enabled`, scale-in one pod / 2 min). `OC_NODE_ID` = pod name.
- **Secrets**: the chart Secret (or `secrets.existingSecret`) is mounted with `envFrom`, so it
  holds `OC_KEK` and every `env:NAME` the hosts file references (JWT secrets, API keys).
  The hosts file itself comes from a ConfigMap (`hosts.toml` or `hosts.existingConfigMap`).
- **Gotenberg**: `gotenberg.enabled` + `mode: deployment` (Service + NetworkPolicy allowing only
  OpenCanvas pods) or `mode: sidecar` (bound to 127.0.0.1 in each pod), or `externalUrl`.
- **Ingress (ingress-nginx)**: one Ingress for `/` (round-robin) and, with
  `ingress.stickyRooms`, a second for `/v1/collab/` with `upstream-hash-by: "$uri"`, so all
  sockets of a room reach the same pod (the owner, fewer relays). 3600 s proxy timeouts,
  buffering off. Other controllers: hash on the path segment after `/v1/collab/`.
- **Drain**: `preStop` sleeps 5 s (endpoints drop the pod), then SIGTERM starts the drain below;
  `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 40` covers the ≤ 30 s commit. PDB `maxUnavailable: 1`.
- Pods run non-root (10001), read-only root, all capabilities dropped, seccomp RuntimeDefault;
  `/tmp` and `/data` are emptyDirs. Probes: liveness `/healthz`, readiness `/readyz`.
- CI (`helm` job) lints and renders single-node SQLite, cluster MariaDB + Redis and
  Gotenberg value sets, and checks SQLite + 2 replicas is refused.

## Cluster (MySQL/MariaDB + Redis, ADR-006)
```
DATABASE_URL=mysql://oc:***@mariadb:3306/opencanvas
REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379                 # enables cluster mode
OC_NODE_ID=node-1                            # default: $HOSTNAME
OC_CLUSTER_ADVERTISE=http://node-1:8080      # how other nodes reach this one (default http://$OC_NODE_ID:<port>)
OC_CLUSTER_SECRET=<≥ 32 chars, same on every node>
OC_KEK=<same on every node>                  # nodes read each other's sealed rows
```
`REDIS_URL` with SQLite refuses to start. Rooms are owned by one node through the Redis
lease `room:{id}:owner` (`SET NX PX 15000`, renewed every 5 s). A node that receives a socket
for a room it does not own relays it to the owner over `/v1/internal/relay/:room`; host-API
room calls go to `/v1/internal/rooms/:room`. **Never expose `/v1/internal/` through the load
balancer**; nodes must reach each other directly.

LB: HTTP round-robin; WebSocket `hash $room consistent` on the `/v1/collab/<room>` path
segment, `proxy_connect_timeout 1s` and `proxy_next_upstream error timeout` so a dead node's
rooms move along the ring (see `deploy/nginx/opencanvas-cluster.conf`).
`docker-compose.cluster.yml` ships 3 nodes + MariaDB + Redis + nginx (`:8580`) + the sample
host (`:4580`). `scripts/chaos-cluster.sh` brings it up, types from two clients, `docker kill`s
the room owner, checks reconnect ≤ 5 s, convergence and that the host's file has every
acknowledged edit, then removes everything.

### Hot WAL in Redis (ADR-028)
```
OC_WAL_REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379   # default: REDIS_URL; also allowed with SQLite (single node)
OC_DB_SYNC_MS=5000                    # DB snapshot per room at most this often (and on close/drain)
OC_DB_SYNC_UPDATES=500                # … or after this many updates
OC_WAL_GROUP_COMMIT=1                 # SQLite without Redis: one writer task, many rooms per commit
```
With a WAL Redis, every edit is appended to the stream `oc:wal:{room}` before anyone sees it,
and **acknowledged means in Redis**. Redis persistence therefore decides what a Redis crash can
lose: `appendonly yes` + `appendfsync always` loses nothing acknowledged (recommended);
`appendfsync everysec` can lose about the last second (acceptable only with a replica you fail
over to); `appendonly no` loses everything since the room's last DB sync (≤ `OC_DB_SYNC_MS`).
The server logs a warning at start-up when `appendonly` is `no` or `appendfsync` is not
`always` (or when `CONFIG GET` is refused). Redis memory per room is the updates since the last
sync (a busy room: a few thousand entries, well under 1 MB). Fencing: the append script refuses
a writer whose epoch is older than `oc:epoch:{room}` (raised at every room claim), and that room
closes with 1012.

## Health & metrics
- `/healthz` — process alive. `/readyz` — DB reachable, (cluster) Redis reachable, not draining.
- `/metrics` (Prometheus): `oc_rooms_live`, `oc_connections{role}`,
  `oc_updates_total`, `oc_update_apply_seconds`, `oc_fanout_bytes_total`,
  `oc_commit_total{result}`, `oc_commit_seconds`, `oc_host_callback_seconds{op,status}`,
  `oc_wal_bytes`, `oc_room_doc_bytes` (histogram), `oc_relay_frames_total`.
- **Implemented today**: `oc_rooms_active`, `oc_connections_active`, `oc_launches_total`,
  `oc_launches_rejected_total`, `oc_updates_total`, `oc_updates_rejected_total`, `oc_saves_total`,
  `oc_save_errors_total`, `oc_save_conflicts_total`, and **`oc_wal_append_seconds`**: a
  histogram (buckets 1 ms … 5 s, plus `_sum` and `_count`) of the time to append one room's
  batch of updates to the WAL, deadlock retries included, success or failure, and
  `oc_wal_batches_total` / `oc_wal_rows_total` (their ratio is the mean batch size). Every
  accepted edit waits for its batch before it is fanned out, so its p95 is the floor of edit
  latency; alert when
  `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(oc_wal_append_seconds_bucket[5m]))` stays above 50 ms (a slow
  or contended database; docs/22 §8 weaknesses 2 and 6). The other names above are planned.
- Logs: JSON, request id, room id, host id; never content.
- Traces: OTLP exporter when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` set.

## Graceful shutdown / deploys
SIGTERM → refuse new rooms → commit all dirty rooms (≤ 20 s each, in parallel) →
`{"t":"reconnect"}` + close 1012 to every client (local and relayed) → release leases → exit.
Rolling deploys move rooms with a ≤ 5 s client reconnect. Give the container a stop grace
period of ≥ 30 s. While draining, `/readyz` answers 503 and new WebSocket upgrades get HTTP 503
with `Retry-After: 5` (refused before the upgrade), so clients and load balancers move on.

## Sizing
Measured on an Apple M4 laptop (10 cores, 16 GB); method, raw tables and caveats in
[22](22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md). Keep ≤ 60 % of measured use.

| Load (small rooms, 20 % typing) | Shape |
|---|---|
| ≤ 1 000 concurrent users | 1 node, 1 vCPU, 512 MB, SQLite |
| ≤ 5 000 concurrent users | 1 node, 2 vCPU, 2 GB, SQLite |
| One room at the 550 cap | 3 vCPU and ≥ 600 Mbit/s for that room |
| Beyond 5 000 | cluster mode (MariaDB + Redis), about one node per 5 000 users (not measured yet) |

Memory ≈ 50 MB + 0.25 MB per user + 5–14× the document per open room. Raise `nofile` above the
connection count. Rerun on your hardware: `scripts/bench.sh`.


# Security and limits

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/security.html
Source file: docs/07-SECURITY-AND-LIMITS.md

**Status:** v0.2, 2026-11-21 (after the security audit, [docs/18](18-SECURITY-AUDIT.md)). Target: OWASP ASVS Level 2.
Reporting a vulnerability: [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md).

## 1. Trust boundaries

```
[end-user browser] ──(untrusted input)──▶ [OpenCanvas] ──(signed calls)──▶ [host]
       ▲                                       │
       └── renders user content (XSS risk) ────┘
[OpenCanvas] ──(fetches arbitrary URLs: unfurl)──▶ [internet]  (SSRF risk)
```

## 2. Threats and controls

| Threat | Control |
|---|---|
| Forged launch token | Per-host key; verify `alg` from host config (never from header), `iss`, `aud`, `exp ≤ 10h`, `nbf`, `jti` single-use cache (DB/Redis). |
| Token leakage via URL | JWT posted in form body, not query; WS uses short (≤ 60 s to connect) single-room ticket; tickets never logged. |
| Privilege escalation (viewer edits) | Server filters every `sync update` by role; commenters restricted to `comments` subtree via scratch-doc diff. Client read-only is cosmetic. |
| Presence spoofing | Server overwrites `awareness.user` from grant. |
| XSS via paste/import/markdown | ProseMirror schema whitelist (paste is parsed by the schema, unknown tags dropped); server HTML import (`oc_model::html`) is a whitelist tree walk, not raw HTML; no raw HTML block; links restricted to `http(s):`, `mailto:`, `/`, `#` (import and export); the link mark re-checks `isAllowedUri` when rendering. |
| Malicious embeds | Provider allow-list per host; `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-presentation allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox">` only for listed providers, rebuilt from the provider id (`resolveEmbed`), never the stored URL; `referrerpolicy=strict-origin-when-cross-origin` (YouTube refuses to play without a referrer); generic iframe not supported. CSP `frame-src https:`. |
| SSRF via image URL / WOPISrc / JWKS | No arbitrary fetches: export images only from the host's `callback_base` origin and `asset_origins` (exact origin match, no userinfo, no redirects, 10 MB, `image/*`); `WOPISrc` only when it matches a `wopi_allowlist` entry exactly (scheme, host, port, path prefix; userinfo, queries and encoded separators refused; no redirects); JWKS and Gotenberg URLs come from operator config. There is no server-side link unfurl; if one is added it must resolve DNS once, pin the IP, block private/link-local/loopback/metadata ranges (v4+v6) and re-check every redirect. |
| Clickjacking / embedding by strangers | CSP `frame-ancestors` = host `allowed_origins`; postMessage origin checks both ways. |
| Script injection into the SPA | Every response: `Content-Security-Policy` with `script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'` (+ `frame-ancestors`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Handler CSPs are kept: exports and room assets are served `sandbox; default-src 'none'`. Node views pass doc URLs through `safeHref` / `safeImageSrc` (`web/packages/editor/src/lib/urls.ts`). |
| Injection into exports | HTML/SVG/DOCX escape every text and attribute; link targets limited to `http(s):`, `mailto:`, `/`, `#`; Markdown escapes `<` and drops script/data link targets; CSV cells starting with `= + - @ TAB CR` get a leading `'`. |
| SQL injection | Every statement is a literal with `?` binds (guard test `sec05_every_sql_statement_is_a_literal`); no dynamic identifiers, no `LIKE`. |
| Callback replay | `X-OpenCanvas-Signature` `v2` binds method + path + query + body; the signed client never follows redirects. |
| Callback spoofing (someone pretends to be us) | HMAC `X-OpenCanvas-Signature` with timestamp (5 min skew). |
| DoS | Per-connection frame rate limits (per-IP limits belong in the reverse proxy); readers that stop reading are dropped (30 s send timeout, 4096-frame backlog); multipart boundaries ≤ 70 chars; frame ≤ 1 MB; doc ≤ 20 MB (block and shape counts are bounded by the doc cap only); room peers ≤ 550 (then close 1013), ≤ 8 awareness client ids per connection; decompression caps on zip import (ratio ≤ 100, total ≤ 100 MB, entries ≤ 1 000, no path traversal), enforced on the bytes actually inflated, never on the sizes the archive declares. |
| Secrets at rest | Host secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted with `OC_KEK`; host callback tokens in `sessions.grant_json` encrypted. |
| Data retention | Room state deleted after commit + TTL; no content in logs (only ids, sizes, timings); crash dumps disabled in prod. |
| Supply chain | `scripts/audit.sh` (`cargo audit`, `cargo deny` with `scripts/deny.toml`, `pnpm audit --prod`), lockfiles, pinned CDN-free bundle (self-hosted assets). |
| Ops endpoints | `/metrics` needs `Authorization: Bearer $OC_METRICS_TOKEN` when set; keep `/metrics`, `/readyz` and `/v1/internal/*` off the public listener. |

## 3. Limits (defaults, per host overridable)

| Limit | Default |
|---|---|
| Launch token TTL max | 10 h |
| WS ticket connect window | 60 s |
| Frame size | 1 MB |
| Frames/s per connection | 60 (burst 120) |
| Awareness size / rate | 2 KB / 20 Hz |
| CRDT doc soft / hard | 5 MB / 20 MB |
| Blocks per doc / shapes per board | bounded by the 20 MB doc cap (no separate count limit) |
| Image upload | 25 MB |
| Attachment upload | host-defined (default 100 MB) |
| Connections per room | 550 (`MAX_PEERS`, not split by role) |
| Unfurl fetch | 2 MB, 5 s, 3 redirects (no server-side unfurl yet: bookmarks store the URL only) |
| Awareness client ids / connection | 8 |
| `GET /v1/users` `q` | 200 bytes |

## 4. Privacy

- PII held in memory only: display name, avatar URL, user id — from the token.
- `sessions` rows hold user id + role until token expiry, then purged hourly.
- GDPR delete is the host's job (they hold the file); we purge on
  `DELETE /v1/files/{id}/session`.


# Capacity and sizing

URL: https://casualoffice.github.io/opencanvas/docs/capacity.html
Source file: docs/22-CAPACITY-AND-SIZING.md

**Status:** first measurement, 2026-11-22 (PERF-01); worst case, crash recovery and cluster
correctness added the same day (PERF-02, §8–§13; read §8's weaknesses before sizing a cluster). Laptop numbers: indicative, not a guarantee.
Rerun on your own hardware with `scripts/bench.sh` (below).

## 1. Machine and method

- **Machine:** Apple M4, 10 cores, 16 GB RAM, macOS 26.3. The server, the load generator and the
  mock host all ran on this one machine, over loopback. The load generator used up to 2.2 cores
  (one room of 550) and 0.6 cores (5,000 connections) next to the server, so the server never had
  the machine to itself.
- **Server:** `opencanvas` release build from main (`7e2de05`), SQLite (`DATABASE_URL=sqlite://…`),
  `OC_KEK` set, `OC_LOG=info`, default limits and autosave (2 s debounce, 10 s max).
- **Load generator:** `crates/oc-bench` (Rust, tokio, tokio-tungstenite, yrs). For each virtual
  user it mints an HS256 launch token for a `bench` host, `POST /v1/launch`, `GET /v1/sessions/<ticket>`
  and opens `/v1/collab/<room>`, like the SPA. The `bench` host's load and save callbacks are served
  by a mock inside the load generator that answers at once, so the host never limits a run.
- **Behaviour:** editors type 3–6 chars/s in bursts of 3–10 s with about 60 % duty, move their
  caret (awareness), and on about 6 % of keystrokes edit a database cell and on 2 % drag a board
  shape (10 moves at 20 Hz). Like the editor, each client sends at most one update frame and one
  awareness frame per 50 ms window. Viewers only receive. Mix: 20 % editors / 80 % viewers.
- **Document:** a Rust rebuild of the "Sprint 42 planning" demo canvas (same blocks, the 7-row
  database, a 12-shape board, one comment thread, a 40 KB inline image): **49 KB** encoded Yjs
  state. `big` adds a 1,000-row database and a 500-shape board: **408 KB** (`oc-bench sizes`).
- **Latency:** every update frame an editor sends is logged by (client id, start clock, time);
  probe clients (4–10 per room) decode each update they receive and look it up. The figure is
  editor frame sent → peer received: server apply, WAL append, fan-out and both sockets. The
  client's own ≤ 50 ms batching window comes on top.
- **Server resources:** `ps` (RSS, CPU time → CPU %, threads), `lsof` (open fds) and `/metrics`
  once per step. CPU % is per core: 100 % = one core busy. Each step ramps clients in, waits 5 s,
  then measures for 60 s (scenario C: 5 s).

## 2. Results

### A. One big room (demo doc, 20 % editors, ramp to the 550 cap)

| clients | editors | p50 ms | p95 ms | p99 ms | server CPU % | RSS MB | fds | updates/s in | frames/s out | MB/s out |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 2 | 0.5 | 5.8 | 10.3 | 0 | 17 | 35 | 7 | 121 | 0.02 |
| 50 | 10 | 0.3 | 0.7 | 1.1 | 2 | 26 | 75 | 32 | 3,049 | 0.55 |
| 100 | 20 | 1.0 | 2.2 | 3.4 | 13 | 37 | 125 | 61 | 11,859 | 2.19 |
| 200 | 40 | 2.1 | 5.2 | 7.1 | 47 | 63 | 225 | 122 | 47,148 | 8.75 |
| 350 | 70 | 1.5 | 3.7 | 4.5 | 73 | 112 | 375 | 207 | 140,878 | 26.61 |
| 550 | 110 | 2.8 | 6.8 | 9.9 | 177 | 193 | 576 | 322 | 345,255 | 65.15 |

No errors, no disconnects, connect (launch → `role`) p95 12 ms at 550. The p95 never came near the
150 ms PRD target; the room cap (550, `MAX_PEERS`) was reached first. Cost grows with the square
